name: Incotex
why: Trousers — chinos, flannels, dress pants — and nothing else, made with tailoring-grade construction.
origin: Founded in Venice in 1951; the founding house of the Slowear group.

notes.cotton: the chino benchmark — the pair the specialty shops fit everything else against
notes.craft: Slowear's about page dates Incotex to a small trouser-making company in the province of Venice in 1951, and its CEO told Forbes in 2018 'we own our factories and are completely vertical'. But slowear.com never names or shows a factory, and only 1 of 8 Incotex product pages says Made in Italy. Kept at 4 on the stated ownership. It cannot be a 5 without a named, current factory. [ruled by Sebastian 4 Oct 2026]
notes.ital: Trousers only, made in the Veneto, and a specialist inside the Slowear group. The narrowness is the point: a house that has spent decades on one garment.

craft_evidence.owned_d: Owned making is claimed but no factory is named. Slowear (the group that owns and sells Incotex) about page: history began 1951 'in the province of Venice' when 'a small production company – Incotex – began its activity, making work trousers'; Slowear S.p.A. address Via della Fornace 15-17, Mira (VE) is given only as company address, not as a factory. 2018 Forbes interview: CEO Roberto Compagno says 'we own our factories and are completely vertical', and the writer calls Slowear 'the only menswear luxury apparel factory in Venice'. Neither slowear.com nor the Incotex page names or shows a trouser factory.
craft_evidence.countries: Italy 1/8 (Blue Division five-pocket: 'Made in Italy trousers'); 7/8 state no country in description, composition or care sections (sample of 8 Incotex PDPs/product data; two rendered pages checked, which have Design & Fit and Care & Composition accordions, so not certain nothing is hidden). Forbes 2018 CEO: 'All our product is made in Europe'.
